key_insight: Human experts and LLMs achieved comparable synthesis success, and their closed-loop collaboration enabled discovery of a new material prototype, Ba3PtO5.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests LLM-assisted recipe generation can accelerate materials synthesis planning and expand discovery in complex chemical phase spaces when paired with experimental validation.
method: Generate synthesis recipes with both humans and LLMs for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper candidates.
Test candidate recipes in the lab and feed results back into a closed-loop human/LLM refinement cycle.
Compare round-one and round-two success rates across known vs. unknown materials.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed similar success rates for humans and LLMs on known materials, but much lower rates on unknown materials, with a closed-loop process ultimately yielding Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply on unknown targets, so LLM outputs still require careful experimental vetting and domain-expert oversight.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
